correctness.rationale: On R_{m,n}=K_m□K_n, the unweighted Laplacian eigenspaces have eigenvalues 0,m,n,m+n and the last space of row/column-sum-zero matrices has dimension q=(m−1)(n−1), forcing ≥q coordinate actuators by PBH. At q actuators the unactuated cell set has m+n−1 edges in bipartite K_{m,n}; PBH on the high eigenspace means its oriented incidence kernel is zero, equivalent to a spanning tree. If m≠n, any forbidden nonzero row/column mode would force two complete rows/columns in a tree and hence a 4-cycle, impossible. If m=n=s the merged middle eigenspace X_ij=x_i+y_j vanishing on actuator graph U is controlled by its connected-component row/column count matrix. Failure iff h≥3 or h=2 with both components balanced, and the extremal edge bound with |U|=(s−1)^2 exhausts just the double stars and cross-plus-one trees, counts s² and s²(s−1)²; all other trees pass. Matrix-tree gives m^{n−1}n^{m−1}. A separate forcing argument gives Z=q+1 (context). An independently written exact modular PBH/tree enumerator verified full cases 3×3,3×4,4×3. Finite checks supplement all-size proof.
